playbook:
When hide stage is put to me, I choose a cell that balances unpredictability and coverage: alternate between center (5) and an off-center choice (3 or 7) rather than always picking the same number; after any confirmed hit on me, move farther from the last hit (pick a different quadrant, not the same or symmetric cell).

When posting a station note, I make a short plausible operational message that neither reveals my hide cell nor blatantly misleads the picket; keep it one concise sentence about sensor/maintenance/status. If I am negotiating an escort, state that intention clearly and in the same round follow through with the salvage claim.

When the standing order tells me which boat to fire on, I follow the standing order unless there is a clear tactical reason not to (e.g., target is Harbor or target is already off the board). I do not deviate lightly from the standing order.

When selecting a firing cell, I avoid repeating the exact same cell every round; vary within a small set of cells consistent with my hide choices to reduce predictability (use the same neighborhood as my hide choices). If I expect a target to be predictable, bias toward cells that historically hit them, but still include occasional variation to prevent exploitation.

When the office privately informs me of my shot result, I truthfully file the public claim to match that private result (claim must equal the office’s private result).

When Harbor is a legal target, I do not fire on Harbor unless I have an explicit plan that accepts the guaranteed 3-point jettison penalty; prefer to never shoot Harbor because the cost is forced and large.

When making escort (salvage) claims, I only name a real live boat that I actively coordinate with or have a credible justification for escorting; avoid inventing names. If I announce a reciprocal escort in my note, I will also file the matching salvage claim that round to secure the mutual 5-point payoff. Do not announce an escort unless I expect the other party to follow through; if coordination fails, retract or avoid claiming mutuality next round.

When I cannot credibly escort anyone, I file [salvage: none] rather than making a risky/false escort claim.

When choosing whether to break standing order for tactical reasons (e.g., to secure an escort partnership or to avoid shooting Harbor), explicitly weigh immediate point gain versus long-term retaliation; only deviate when the benefit is clear and I will act consistently with any public statements I make.

When tracking other boats’ patterns (notes, hides, claims), I adjust my hide and firing cells to exploit consistent predictable behavior from them; if they vary, match that variance rather than staying fixed. Record hits and misses on targets to build a short model of their likely hide cells and update firing bias accordingly.

When a previous shot on me was a hit, I change my hide cell pattern more aggressively next round (move farther from last known hits) and avoid repeating the same cell or small neighborhood.

When posting notes, avoid verbose technical jargon that could be used to infer my location or intentions; keep notes operational and ambiguous. Use notes to set up credible escort coordination when beneficial, and remember to act on those notes during salvage stage.

When in doubt about any claim or escort, favor honesty and minimal exposure: truthful shot claims, and no escort if unverifiable. If I coordinate an escort, ensure the other party has signaled intent before claiming mutual to avoid lost credibility.

1.text:
When asked to hide, I generally choose a central cell early in the patrol to maximize firing flexibility and cover. If an opponent repeatedly targets me, I will relocate by at least 2–3 cells on my next hide (not just adjacent) and vary hide choices thereafter to break predictability. Late in the patrol I favor less-central, less-predictable hides if opponents have learned my central bias.

When posting a station note, I give a short, plausible technical/status line that reveals nothing about hide, shots, or intents (e.g., diagnostics/status/monitoring). Notes must be concise and noncommittal; do not disclose coordinates, targets, or signaling intentions.

When the standing order names my target, I follow it by default unless there is a clear tactical reason not to (e.g., target is Harbor and firing would jettison me, or following the order would create an obvious exploitable pattern). If the standing order repeatedly exposes predictable behavior that harms me, I will consider a safe deviation (shift hide or vary firing cell) to reduce exploitation.

When selecting a firing cell, use any observed hit/miss history to narrow probable opponent positions; a confirmed hit pins a boat’s hide and should be exploited in subsequent rounds. If no useful information exists, choose a cell that preserves flexibility (central or one that complements my hide) rather than an arbitrary extreme.

When the office privately reports my shot result, I always file the required public claim honestly and exactly (hit or miss). Honest claims prevent internal inconsistencies other players can exploit and preserve my credibility for any future coordination.

When considering firing on Harbor, avoid doing so except as part of an explicit, high-value plan: Harbor penalties are costly and often counterproductive. Treat firing on Harbor as a last-resort tactical choice, not a routine action.

When naming an escort, claim a boat only if I reasonably expect reciprocal naming (direct, clear mutual signaling or very strong behavioral cues). If reciprocal escort is unlikely, name none. Do not fabricate escort claims; false claims risk contradiction and loss of credibility. When safe mutual escort is arranged, use it to secure the mutual 5-point bonus.

When I am hit by another boat, assume they know my cell and move on the next hide. After being hit, deprioritize remaining in place or making small moves that keep me predictable.

When uncertain about opponents’ positions or intents, prioritize information-preserving actions: honest claims, neutral notes, conservative escort choices, and hide moves that preserve options rather than bluffing in ways that create exploitable inconsistencies.

When making any public text (notes, claims, escort declarations), keep wording concise, technical, and nonrevealing; never leak timing, exact coordinates, or admission of strategic intent.

Maintain flexibility in tactics: early patrol = central hides and information-gathering; mid/late patrol = adapt hides and firing to observed patterns, break predictability, and exploit any confirmed hits.

2.text:
When asked to hide, choose a cell unpredictably. I will bias away from extreme edges only when I have no other corroborating signal; otherwise I randomize uniformly among 1–9. I will avoid making the same exact hide-cell choice in two immediately consecutive hides unless I have an explicit reason to do so (e.g., confirmed pattern from opponents).

When I must follow a standing firing order, fire at the next live station as ordered (Echo → Foxtrot → Gamma cycle when I am Gamma). If the standing order would require firing on Harbor, treat Harbor as off-limits by default and refuse unless I deliberately accept the guaranteed jettison penalty and its point transfer.

When selecting a cell to fire, randomize my aim across the nine cells rather than use a predictable sequence. If I have reasoned, corroborated suspicion about a station’s likely location from multiple independent public signals, I will modestly weight selections toward that area but keep randomness so opponents cannot deduce my pattern. I will avoid repeatedly firing the identical cell in successive rounds without new evidence.

When the office privately tells me my shot result, I will always file the claim that exactly matches that private result (hit or miss). I will never fabricate a private-result claim.

When posting my station note, I will stick to operational/administrative content and coordination proposals only. I will not reveal or imply my hide cell, intended target cell, or the private shot result. I will use the note stage to attempt explicit, clear coordination (for example, proposing a bilateral escort with a named live boat).

Escort coordination and claiming:
- To try to earn escort points, I will explicitly propose a bilateral escort to a single chosen live picket boat (never Harbor) in the note stage, naming that partner clearly.
- I will only file an escort claim for a round if that named partner publicly reciprocates in the same round (mutual naming). If there is no public reciprocation that round, I will file [salvage: none].
- When escort points are likely to decide the outcome (scores close late), I will prioritize securing a single reliable bilateral escort with one consistent partner rather than trying to court multiple partners at once.
- I will never claim an escort with a non-player or made-up name.

When making escort claims, name only a live picket boat (not Harbor). If a partner publicly reciprocates in the same round, I will file the matching escort claim immediately; if the partner reciprocates in a later round, I will not retroactively claim the earlier round.

When the score situation makes risk-taking unattractive (I am leading late in the patrol or near a win), I will favor conservative choices: avoid firing Harbor, concentrate on securing escort points via explicit reciprocal signals, and maintain nondeterministic hiding and firing so opponents cannot easily target me.

When I detect anomalies or odd phrasing in notes, I will log them succinctly for the public record (e.g., “noted unusual telemetry wording”) but will not change my hiding/firing pattern in an obvious way that could reveal my location. I will prefer to interpret single unusual notes cautiously and only update suspicion weights when multiple independent signals corroborate.

When rounds are late and point standings are close, I will emphasize escort coordination and safe firing (avoid Harbor). If I am trailing and need points, I will accept more aggressive firing to try for hits, but still avoid predictable aiming patterns.

When the office validates inputs, ensure coordinates are integers 1–9 and claims use exact allowed tokens; format responses strictly as required.

When tempted to fabricate an escort or claim an escort without reciprocity, do not do it—false escort claims are unlikely to score and will erode trust for future coordination.

When tempted to fire Harbor to steal its payroll, remember Harbor’s standing signal and the guaranteed jettison consequence; only fire Harbor if the strategic calculus explicitly values the jettisoned points over survival.

Keep a short consistent partnership preference list (one preferred partner, one backup). Use the note stage each round to attempt to maintain the same partner if mutual escort payoffs have been earned previously; this increases the chance of reciprocation. If a partner fails to reciprocate repeatedly, drop them and try to form a bilateral with a different live boat.

Revise targeting weights only when independent evidence supports it: multiple hits/misses patterns or communal notes pointing to a consistent sector. Otherwise preserve randomness to avoid giving opponents exploitable patterns.
